acceptance.accepted_history_rule: Only the event exactly anchored by CURRENT.latest_event commit+path+digest is accepted history.
acceptance.duplicate_rule: Existing deterministic claim path is DUPLICATE; do not replace claim, outbox, event, or CURRENT.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Second CURRENT fetch must remain exact v64/blob 618c247adfe218b9c9f01007c8785516d9dc9eb5/projection digest 0502ac09582d6ba91f6b1b6833453e8422b9e2f1ae5f743a9862ae5e530367f7 before one blob-SHA-guarded replacement; final readback must be v65.
acceptance.slack_gate: Slack post is prohibited before version advance. Recovery scan may post only after final CURRENT readback anchors this exact event path and digest.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is a same-run recovery simulation, not a real process crash. The claim, outbox intent, event, CURRENT replacement, final read, Slack post, and delivery receipt are separate effects. A crash after Slack accepts the post but before the receipt is committed can cause duplicate recovery delivery. Git provides no cross-file transaction, database isolation or uniqueness, linearizability, exactly-once execution, force-push safety, cross-branch exclusion, or Slack atomicity.

probe.name: DURABLE_OUTBOX_RECOVERY_SCAN_AFTER_INTENTIONAL_IMMEDIATE_POST_SKIP_V1
probe.result: A create-only pending Slack outbox intent was created and read back before CURRENT. The immediate Slack path was intentionally skipped; after exact v65 final readback, a recovery scan must use this outbox to post one sanitized pointer and append an immutable delivery receipt.

canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the claim, outbox, event, or receipt. If v65 is later invalid, append a compensating transition from the then-current exact version; if Slack delivery is wrong or duplicated, append a correction receipt without rewriting prior evidence.
